svg.title: Two Pointers
svg.desc: Two Pointers. Move two indices through an array, toward each other or one chasing the other, to solve pair and partition problems in one pass. Step 1, Every pair: O(n²): Two nested loops try every pair in turn: 11 + 14 = 25 turns up on check 23, out of 28 pairs. Step 2, Squeeze from both ends: On a sorted array, a sum too small moves lo right and one too big moves hi left: 7 checks, not 23. Step 3, Why nothing is missed: A sum too small rules out lo's whole row of pairs, too big hi's whole column: all 28 in 7 checks. Step 4, Same direction: dedupe: Both move right: r reads each value and w writes each new one, leaving 1 2 3 4 5 in front.

g.text: Two nested loops try every pair in turn: 11 + 14 = 25 turns up on check 23, out of 28 pairs.
On a sorted array, a sum too small moves lo right and one too big moves hi left: 7 checks, not 23.
A sum too small rules out lo's whole row of pairs, too big hi's whole column: all 28 in 7 checks.
Both move right: r reads each value and w writes each new one, leaving 1 2 3 4 5 in front.
Find a pair that sums to 25
one cell per pair, i < j:
k = 5: one copy of each value

text.tspan: · swap the two ends, then step both inward
· merge sort's merge, a database merge join
· find a cycle in a linked list (Floyd)

g.text: if a[i] + a[j] == 25: return i, j
Each failed pair dims its cell in the grid.
Every pair of 8 values is 8 × 7 / 2 = 28 checks.
Two pointers: squeeze from both ends
Sum too small: move lo right, to a bigger value.
Sum too big: move hi left, to a smaller value.
Each check moves one pointer inward: at most n − 1.
Too small: a[lo] + any value left is too small → row out.
Too big: any value left + a[hi] is too big → column out.
All 28 pairs are checked or ruled out: none is missed.
r reads a[1] to a[8]. If a[r] ≠ the last kept value a[w − 1],
copy it to a[w] and move w one step right.
O(1) extra space: the array is rewritten in place.
